title: Fix stale Rust-port URLs and package metadata that point to the Python repo
description:
## Problem

Several user-facing metadata paths still point to the original Python repository rather than this Rust port:

- The Rust CLI welcome banner prints `Docs : https://github.com/hexo-ai/sia` (`src/bin/sia.rs:21-23`).
- The Python package metadata also uses `https://github.com/hexo-ai/sia` for Homepage and Repository (`pyproject.toml:48-50`).
- The README itself points to this repo's umbrella issue (`README.md:3-10`), so the project identity is mixed.

## Impact

Judges or users who run `sia --help` and click the docs/repo URL may land on the original Python project instead of the Rust hackathon submission. That creates avoidable confusion about what was built, where issues live, and what code is being judged.

## Acceptance criteria

- Update the Rust CLI banner to point to `https://github.com/micahstubbs/sia_rust` or the most appropriate Rust-port docs page.
- Update `pyproject.toml` URLs or intentionally document why the Python package remains tied to the upstream project.
- Add/adjust a lightweight test or snapshot check so the banner/package metadata cannot drift back silently.
- Confirm `cargo run -- --help` shows the intended Rust-port URL.

title: Allow --task arithmetic-mc or stop documenting it as bundled
description:
## Problem

`arithmetic-mc` is present under `sia/tasks/` and is documented as a runnable example, but the Rust CLI rejects it as a bundled task.

Evidence:

- `docs/HACKATHON_DECK.md:298-307` tells users to run `--task arithmetic-mc`.
- `docs/TASK_AUTHORING.md:10-18` says `sia/tasks/arithmetic-mc/` is a complete runnable example.
- The Rust bundled-task allow-list excludes it: `src/layout.rs:10-11` only lists `gpqa`, `lawbench`, `longcot-chess`, and `spaceship-titanic`.
- The CLI binds `--task` to that allow-list (`src/cli.rs:29-33`), and `cargo run -- run --help` only shows those four possible values.

## Impact

This blocks the most obvious small-task fallback for a hackathon demo. It also makes the documentation look untested: judges or teammates who copy the arithmetic command will hit a parser error before the run starts.

## Acceptance criteria

- Either add `arithmetic-mc` to `BUNDLED_TASKS` and update CLI tests/help snapshots, or remove/replace every doc path that presents it as a bundled `--task` value.
- Add a regression test that `parse_args(... --task arithmetic-mc)` succeeds if the task remains documented as bundled.
- Run `cargo run -- run --help` and confirm `arithmetic-mc` appears in possible values, or confirm the docs only use `--task_dir` for it.

title: Rust Port: Overall Migration Plan, Phases, and Tracking (Umbrella)
description:
This is the central tracking issue for the Rust port of SIA.

## Current State (June 6, 2026, evening)

**PR #10 merged successfully.** Solid foundation in place (orchestrator, context, web, Python target bridge, parity tests).

**Core LLM client work (#50 + #51) completed.** The native `AgentRunner` + trajectory logging middleware on rig-core are now implemented. Meta/Feedback agents can now call LLMs natively with high-fidelity trajectory capture.

**Hackathon mode activated.** We have created a focused set of high-value issues (#62–#69) specifically to maximize our chances of winning the Self Improving AI Agents hackathon on Saturday.

## Hackathon Prioritization (New Issues #62–#69)

**Tier 1 — Must have for any winning live demo (do these first)**
1. **#62** — Complete Native End-to-End LLM Client + Rig-Core Integration (blocks everything live)
2. **#63** — "SIA Studio" — Polished Interactive Live Demo Dashboard (the "wow" factor for 3-4 min demos)
3. **#68** — Hackathon Demo Preparation & Judging Narrative (critical delivery piece)

**Tier 2 — High leverage for sponsor alignment + polish**
4. **#64** — Nebius GPU + Multi-Model + Telemetry Integration
5. **#69** — Nebius Token Factory / GPU credits quickstart + model endpoint documentation

**Tier 3 — Strong differentiators (Research / Framework / Applied angles)**
6. **#65** — Adaptive Harness/Weight Scheduler (direct paper extension)
7. **#66** — Impressive Domain Task Templates + Robust Verifier Layer
8. **#67** — Security/Sandbox Hardening + Formal Threat Model

**Future / Strategic**
- **#19** — LoRA / Weight Update Integration (now **Native Rust preferred**; Python bridge to be deprecated long-term). Design work can start; implementation after core loop is proven stable.

## Why this prioritization wins
- Enables a real, live, visible self-improvement loop on Saturday.
- Delivers a polished, judge-friendly demo experience (SIA Studio + narrative).
- Leverages the sponsor (Nebius) directly.
- Includes clear research extension of the paper itself.
- Keeps scope realistic for a one-day hackathon while still being impressive.

## Suggested Implementation Order for the Next 18 Hours
1. Get #62 (native LLM loop) to a working state (even if rough) — this unblocks all live demos.
2. Parallel: Start #63 (SIA Studio) UI polish + #68 (demo script/narrative).
3. Add #64 + #69 (Nebius) so we can run on real H200s with nice telemetry.
4. Add one strong differentiator from Tier 3 (#65 or #66 recommended).
5. Have a rehearsed 3-4 minute demo + narrative ready by Saturday morning.

All new hackathon issues (#62–#69) have been created with detailed bodies, dependencies, suggested approaches, and cross-references back to this umbrella (#34) and the LLM epic (#38).

## Previous Grooming Notes (still valid)
- #19 updated to Native Rust preferred + Python bridge deprecation goal.
- Old broad issues closed during earlier grooming passes.

All decisions and status updates must be commented on the relevant issues for full auditability. Link new work back to this umbrella.

title: Drain native Bash tool output while enforcing timeout
description:
Source: `docs/reviews/codebase-review-2026-06-06.md` finding H2.

The native LLM `Bash` tool pipes stdout/stderr but waits for process exit before reading either stream. Verbose commands can block on full OS pipe buffers and then false-timeout.

Acceptance criteria:
- `tools::bash` drains stdout/stderr while the child is running.
- Timeout still kills/reaps the shell command.
- Regression test covers output substantially larger than a pipe buffer.

title: Add wall-clock timeout to target-agent execution
description:
Source: `docs/reviews/codebase-review-2026-06-06.md` finding M1.

Rust and Python define target/sandbox timeout settings, but target-agent execution waits indefinitely. A generated agent that hangs can hang the entire run.

Acceptance criteria:
- Rust target-agent execution enforces a wall-clock timeout and preserves partial logs.
- Python target-agent execution enforces a wall-clock timeout and preserves partial logs.
- Tests cover timeout behavior for non-Docker execution and Docker command/timeout plumbing where practical.

title: Propagate Rust generated requirements install failures
description:

- Target execution does not continue silently after install failure.
- Regression test covers the failure path.

title: Fix Rust eval timeout to kill evaluator process
description:
Source: `docs/reviews/codebase-review-2026-06-06.md` finding H1.

`run_command_with_timeout` reports `TimedOut` after `eval_timeout`, but it moves the child process into a worker thread and no longer has a handle to kill/reap it. A timed-out `evaluate.py` can continue running and mutate generation artifacts after the orchestrator has moved on.

Acceptance criteria:
- Timeout path kills and reaps the evaluator process.
- Timeout outcome remains explicit in the evaluation result.
- Regression test covers a child process that would otherwise outlive the timeout.

title: Make the Docker sandbox story usable for LLM-calling target agents
description:
## Problem

The demo script presents `--sandbox docker` as the safety answer for generated Python target agents:

- `docs/HACKATHON_DEMO.md:107-112` says adding `--sandbox docker` gives the Python target agent a container with `--network none`, read-only datasets, and CPU/memory caps.
- `build_sandbox_cmd` does exactly that: `--network none`, `/data:ro`, `/work:rw`, and `python:3.11-slim` (`src/orchestrator.rs:270-292`; default image at `src/config.rs:76-80`).
- The normal non-Docker path uses a local venv with baseline packages like `openai`, `google-genai`, `pandas`, and `numpy` (`src/config.rs:88-100`; venv setup in `src/run_setup.rs:201-202`). The Docker command does not mount that venv, install those deps, or pass provider API-key env vars.

That creates a demo tension: the sandbox is safer, but an LLM-calling target agent generally needs network egress, credentials, and Python deps. With `--network none` and no env injection, the Docker mode is not a drop-in safe version of the live Nebius/Gemini target path.

## Impact

If a judge asks to see the sandboxed path, it may fail for the exact tasks/profiles used in the demo. Conversely, if we only use `--sandbox none`, the safety story is much weaker.

## Acceptance criteria

- Decide and document the intended Docker mode clearly: offline-only target agents, or controlled provider egress.
- If offline-only: update hackathon docs to say Docker is for replay/offline target tasks and should not be used with live provider-calling targets unless custom image/network/env are configured.
- If live-provider support is intended: add explicit env allow-listing for required provider keys, dependency installation or a documented demo image, and a network policy that is tighter than unrestricted host execution.
- Add at least one integration-style test or script that runs a tiny target agent under `--sandbox docker` and verifies the advertised constraints plus successful execution.

---

title: Real weight updates — current path is a CPU reference toy, not actual model training
description:
## Gap (found in self-review)
`src/weights.rs` `LoraReferenceUpdater::update` runs synthetic `f64` gradient descent over a hashed bag-of-bytes embedding and writes a `weight_update.json` loss artifact. It is explicitly a **CPU reference** — it does **not** update any real model weights, and the produced "adapter" is never loaded by the target agent. The intended Candle backend (`weights-gpu` / `candle-core` + `candle-nn`) is documented but **not added** (candle isn't in the offline cargo cache).

## Fix
Implement a real weight-update path driven by `extract_training_examples(trajectory, reward)`:
- **Native:** add the `weights-gpu` cargo feature with a `CandleLoraUpdater` implementing `WeightUpdater` (real LoRA fine-tune on a small open model), pinned to a fetchable Candle version, and
- **/or Python bridge:** a test-time-training step (the original Python SIA had one) as an interim, behind a feature/flag.
Produce a real adapter artifact and wire it so the next generation's target agent loads it. Keep the CPU reference as an offline-test fallback.

Refs: #19, #84, scheduler-drives-loop issue, umbrella #34.

title: Add collision-proof run IDs for rehearsal and stage demos
description:
## Problem

The demo commands use fixed run IDs, but the run setup aborts if the directory already exists:

- Pre-demo warm run: `--run_id 0` (`docs/HACKATHON_DEMO.md:42-49`, `docs/HACKATHON_DEMO.md:356-360`).
- Live run: `--run_id 1` (`docs/HACKATHON_DEMO.md:81-88`).
- CLI default is also `--run_id 1` (`src/cli.rs:22-28`).
- `setup_run_directory` returns an error when `./runs/run_<id>` already exists (`src/run_setup.rs:185-193`).

A second rehearsal or a restarted stage command can fail before any interesting demo behavior happens.

## Impact

This is easy to hit during practice and easy to forget on stage. It also makes the default command brittle: a previous `runs/run_1` artifact turns a live demo into a cleanup exercise.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add a collision-proof mode such as `--run_id auto`, `--next-run-id`, or a timestamp-based default suitable for demos.
- Print the selected run directory before starting expensive LLM work.
- Optionally add explicit `--overwrite` / `--resume` behavior, but avoid accidental deletion by default.
- Update hackathon docs to use the collision-proof path for rehearsals and the live run.
- Add tests for existing-directory behavior and the new auto-ID path.

title: Implement or remove the documented SIA_RUNS_DIR run-output override
description:
## Problem

The deck says users can select a specific run output root for `sia run` with `SIA_RUNS_DIR`, but the Rust code appears to hard-code `./runs`:

- `docs/HACKATHON_DECK.md:294-295` says there is no `--runs-dir` flag for `run`; use `SIA_RUNS_DIR` if needed.
- The live dashboard background server is always started with `names::RUNS_ROOT` (`src/run.rs:54-59`).
- `setup_run_directory` always calls `RunLayout::for_run_id(..., names::RUNS_ROOT)` (`src/run_setup.rs:185-188`).
- `Config::from_env` documents and implements only the parity-preserving env overrides; `SIA_RUNS_DIR` is not one of them (`src/config.rs:102-134`).
- `src/layout.rs:29` defines `RUNS_ROOT` as `./runs`.

## Impact

A presenter trying to isolate rehearsal artifacts, use a prerecorded runs directory, or avoid collisions by setting `SIA_RUNS_DIR` will get surprising behavior. The docs suggest a mitigation that does not currently exist.

## Acceptance criteria

- Either implement a supported run-output override for `sia run` (`SIA_RUNS_DIR`, `--runs-dir`, or similar), or remove the `SIA_RUNS_DIR` guidance from the hackathon deck.
- Ensure the auto-started dashboard serves the same root that `sia run` is writing to.
- Add tests covering the selected run root and the web server root for live runs.
- Update `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/HACKATHON_DECK.md`, and any related run/replay docs to use one consistent mechanism.

title: Add a stage-safe live demo command instead of GPQA max_gen=3
description:
## Problem

The live run-of-show asks the presenter to run a 3-generation GPQA demo during the 1:00-2:30 segment:

- `docs/HACKATHON_DEMO.md:76-88` uses `--task gpqa --max_gen 3` as the live command.
- The pre-demo checklist uses the same GPQA 3-generation warm run (`docs/HACKATHON_DEMO.md:356-360`).
- GPQA currently has 198 public questions, and the reference-style flow does provider calls per question (`sia/tasks/gpqa/data/public/diamond_questions.json`; `sia/tasks/gpqa/reference/reference_target_agent.py:121-170`).
- The deck itself admits GPQA generations take minutes, not seconds (`docs/HACKATHON_DECK.md:333-344`).

Hackathon judging rubrics commonly score technical implementation and presentation/demo quality. A command that is expected to take minutes per generation is not a reliable 3-4 minute stage demo path.

## Impact

The live demo can stall on provider latency, quota, or long per-question execution. That forces the presenter to abandon the promised live run and jump to prerecorded artifacts, which is acceptable as a backup but weak as the primary path.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add and document a primary stage-safe command that reliably shows a full generation cycle within the allotted time on a fresh demo machine.
- Prefer a tiny bundled task or smoke task with 3-5 examples and deterministic/easy scoring.
- Keep GPQA as the research/credibility path, but demote it to warm-run or offline replay unless measured runtime supports the script.
- Update `docs/HACKATHON_DEMO.md` and `docs/HACKATHON_DECK.md` so the run-of-show, checklist, and runtime guidance agree.
- Include a measured runtime note from an actual rehearsal run.

title: Live end-to-end validation — every integration's real path is only covered by #[ignore] tests
description:
## Gap (found in self-review)
All offline/mock tests pass, but **no real network call or full `sia run` self-improvement loop has ever been executed**. Every live path is gated behind `#[ignore]` + an env key:

- `src/llm/claude_runner.rs::live_native_loop_end_to_end` (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
- `src/llm/openhands_runner.rs::live_openhands_loop_end_to_end` (provider key)
- `src/llm/pydantic_ai_runner.rs::live_pydantic_ai_loop_end_to_end` (provider key)
- `src/llm/rig_runner.rs::live_single_turn` (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
- `src/llm/structured.rs::live_structured_extract` (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
- `tests/nebius_live.rs::bundled_nebius_profile_slugs_exist_in_live_catalog` (NEBIUS_API_KEY)

## Fix
With real keys, run all `#[ignore]`d live tests (`cargo test --features llm -- --ignored`) **and** a complete `cargo run --features llm -- run …` on a bundled task (e.g. `arithmetic-mc` or `gpqa`), capture the results/artifacts, and fix anything that breaks (auth, request shape, tool-loop, trajectory write, evaluation). This is the gate that turns "all the pieces compile and pass mocks" into "the loop actually works."

Refs: #62, supply-keys issue, umbrella #34.

title: Scheduler decision is observational only — make it actually drive the generation loop
description:
## Gap (found in self-review)
#84 wires `closed_loop::record_scheduler_decision` / `maybe_run_weight_update` into `run_generation_with` (`src/orchestrator.rs:689`), but both calls are best-effort `let _ =` that only **write artifacts + print a log line**. The orchestrator still performs a harness update every generation regardless of the decision, and the "weight" branch runs a reference toy (see companion issue) that never changes the target agent. The "closed loop" is therefore *visible* but not *acting*.

## Fix
Make the loop branch on the decision: `harness` → current meta-agent harness update; `weight` → run a real weight update (see companion issue) and skip/short-circuit the harness step; `both` → do both. Feed the decision + weight-update outcome into the Feedback-Agent context so the next generation is informed, and surface the *acted* decision (not just the recommendation) in `improvement.md`/SIA Studio.

Depends on: real weight updates (companion issue). Refs: #65, #84, #19, umbrella #34.

title: Add a hardened native-runner capability profile for demo safety
description:
## Problem

The demo safety pitch says native runner tool calls go through a deny-by-default capability allow-list:

- `docs/HACKATHON_DEMO.md:107-112` says every native runner tool call goes through `src/sandbox.rs`, deny-by-default, with a single auditable enforcement point.
- The actual runtime profile used by the Claude runner is `Capabilities::agent_default(wd)` (`src/llm/claude_runner.rs:211-216`; same pattern in other native runners).
- `agent_default` enables read, write, and Bash, and sets `allowed_bash_prefixes = None` (`src/sandbox.rs:136-158`).
- `check_bash` allows any command when no prefix list is present (`src/sandbox.rs:228-248`).
- `tools::bash` executes `sh -c <command>` in the working directory (`src/llm/tools.rs:75-88`).
- `SECURITY.md:63-69` honestly states that native Bash runs arbitrary shell commands with no command allow-list or network restriction.

So the threat model is honest, but the stage pitch can sound stronger than the shipped default. A judge can reasonably ask whether a prompt-injected task can run `curl`, read env vars via Bash, or execute destructive commands.

## Impact

This is a credibility risk for the Framework Enhancement / safety narrative. The code has the policy abstraction needed for a stronger mode, but the default agent profile is permissive enough that "deny-by-default" is not the right phrase for the live native runner behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add a clearly named hardened/native-demo capability profile or CLI/config option that disables Bash or constrains it with `allowed_bash_prefixes`.
- Ensure the native runners can select that profile without code edits.
- Add tests showing dangerous Bash commands are denied in hardened mode and ordinary needed commands still work if explicitly allowed.
- Update `docs/HACKATHON_DEMO.md`, `SECURITY.md`, and related docs so the pitch distinguishes current default mode, hardened demo mode, and roadmap OS-level isolation.

title: Make SIA Studio auto-refresh during live runs
description:
## Problem

The hackathon run-of-show says the SIA Studio dashboard updates in real time while a run is live:

- `docs/HACKATHON_DEMO.md:99-101` says generations appear as they land, the accuracy chart climbs, and telemetry updates in real time.
- The current static UI fetches `/api/runs` once at boot, caches run details in `RUN_CACHE`, and does not poll or invalidate the cache (`sia/web/static/index.html:320-377`).
- The scheduler panel comment explicitly says the file-backed view reflects new decisions only after refresh / re-navigation (`sia/web/static/index.html:494-499`).

For a live judging demo, this means the terminal can be progressing while the browser appears stale unless the presenter manually refreshes or changes routes.

## Impact

This directly weakens the demo promise: judges may not see generation, score, or telemetry updates land live. It also makes the UI look less robust than the underlying file-backed API.

## Acceptance criteria

- While viewing a run, the UI refreshes run detail, generation list, metrics, telemetry, and scheduler panels on a short interval, without losing the selected generation/tab.
- The sidebar run list updates when new `run_*` directories appear.
- The polling path is disabled or throttled when the tab is hidden.
- Add a focused web/UI test or documented manual verification: start `sia web`, add/update a generation artifact under `runs/`, and confirm the visible chart/list updates without page reload.

title: Fail visibly or choose a fallback port when auto-starting the dashboard
description:
## Problem

`sia run` auto-starts the web dashboard, but bind failures can be hidden:

- `run_orchestrator` starts the background server and ignores the return value (`src/run.rs:54-59`).
- `serve_in_background` spawns a thread, discards the result of `serve(...)`, and prints `Live dashboard: http://{host}:{port}` regardless of whether binding succeeds (`src/web/server.rs:226-241`).
- `serve` itself returns an error if the port cannot bind (`src/web/server.rs:215-223`).
- The hackathon script assumes `http://127.0.0.1:8000` is available during the live run (`docs/HACKATHON_DEMO.md:90-101`).

If port 8000 is occupied, the CLI can claim the dashboard is live while the browser fails to load.

## Impact

This is a classic stage-demo failure: the terminal appears fine, the presenter switches to the browser, and nothing is serving. It is also hard to diagnose because the failure happens in a background thread.

## Acceptance criteria

- Before printing the dashboard URL, confirm the listener actually bound successfully.
- Either fail the run visibly with an actionable error, or automatically choose the next available port and print the actual URL.
- Preserve `--web-port` semantics: if the user explicitly requested a port, decide whether to fail hard or opt into fallback with a separate flag.
- Add a test or small harness that occupies a port and verifies `sia run` does not falsely report a live dashboard at that port.
